bullets.title: NVDA: CEO crisis dominates — Jensen ouster, export controls, PT cuts ahead of Tuesday earnings
bullets.body: Jensen Huang's ousting as NVDA CEO is the week's dominant story: Bessent pushed for an external hire, interim CEO Colette Kress is expected to curb startup/infrastructure financing, and Congress is accelerating chip export restrictions. UBS's Arcuri cut PT to $240 (from $300), trimming FY28 revenue to $885B and EPS to $20.01 on ~10% revenue-at-risk from Singapore/Malaysia restrictions; Evercore models 8x P/E and a $100 target on cycle peak thesis. Despite the noise, NVDA is expected to beat FQ3 by ~$3-4B (~$111-112B) and guide FQ4 to ~$130B — the question is whether a new CEO will honor existing ecosystem commitments that underpin neoclouds and indie-lab demand.

bullets.title: NVDA: Pre-market down 3.5-4.4% Monday on leadership/export overhang; semis broadly lower
bullets.body: NVDA opened Monday premarket -3.5% to -4.4% with semis broadly sold: MU -6.2%, MRVL -6.1%, AMD -5.3%, AVGO -4.1%, COHR -7.0%, LITE -6.9%, CIEN -5.4%. NVDA has the lowest 14-day RSI since 2019 (24) and trades at 11x forward earnings. Retail bought $1.6B NVDA on Thursday (10x the next-most-bought name) but HF net-selling streak in semis is the longest on record (6 consecutive weeks, global L/S ratio collapsed from 4.4x to 2.1x).

bullets.title: DELL & HPE: Multiple desks bullish into earnings — beat-and-raise setups on AI server/storage demand
bullets.body: Citi, Morgan Stanley, and UBS all lean constructive on DELL and HPE ahead of results. DELL is down 30%+ to COVID-era trough valuations and is expected to beat Q3 on AI server/storage demand with Jan Q guide potentially above consensus; MS PT $403. HPE backed by healthy enterprise infrastructure spending and buyback return in F4Q; MS PT $64, Citi Buy. Key risk: PC demand deteriorated significantly in C3Q on negative IDC data and Intel earnings, and HPE faces an October Q revenue miss and FY27 EPS guide-down risk.

bullets.title: SMTC: Oppenheimer bullish; DC revenue to 2x, targeting 75% CAGR to $2.1B by CY29; UBS trims PT to $200
bullets.body: Oppenheimer reiterates SMTC with $225 PT, noting DC sales should more than double this year and next with ACC ramping at a top CSP (believed Google) and 2x ASP premiums on 1.6T/3.2T solutions. SMTC trades at 11x CY28E EPS vs AI peers at 15x. UBS trims PT from $230 to $200 (maintains Buy) modeling Oct Q revenue of $418M/$1.14 EPS, guiding toward $440-445M; DC revenue modeled up 130%/120% Y/Y in FY27/FY28 with gross margin exiting FY27 ~60% inflecting to ~65% in FY28.

bullets.title: AMD & TXN: Relative semi safe havens — both held 200-day MAs as preferred semi buys
bullets.body: Oppenheimer and Opco technicals both flag AMD and TXN as the two semiconductors that maintained their 200-day moving averages despite broader sector weakness, designating them as preferred buys. AMD +18.9% and AVGO +18% over 5 days post-NVDA news are seen as beneficiaries of ecosystem rotation. UBS prefers TXN for operating leverage and cycle torque; KeyBanc notes ON and TXN are closing the data-center power management gap but neither is yet qualified at NVDA on Rubin.

bullets.title: RBLX: Piper bullish on AI content tailwind; JPM tracker shows engagement softening W/W, -14% Y/Y
bullets.body: Piper reiterates bullish view: AI is accelerating game supply (new games with first-time ads up 5x), GTA6 headwind is modest, age-verification risk smaller than feared, and Roblox Everywhere is underappreciated. JPM's weekly tracker shows peak CCUs -2% W/W to 23.1M and -14% Y/Y November-to-date; 4Q bookings guide of -15% to -10% Y/Y already factors in GTA VI console-only release. 80%+ of top-100 creators now use AI tools and asset uploads tripled in October.

bullets.title: HUBS: CEO Halligan buys 23K shares at $217.25 after returning as CEO; guidance reaffirmed
bullets.body: HUBS co-founder Brian Halligan purchased ~23K shares at $217.25 (Form 4) after being appointed CEO following Yamini Rangan's departure on Nov 12. Halligan now beneficially owns ~436K shares. CFO Kate Bueker retires Feb 2027; Karen Burgess (Adobe) joins as EVP Finance Nov 30. Company reaffirmed Q4 and FY2026 financial guidance. RBC lists HUBS in a 'questions remain' bucket post-Q3 software earnings bifurcation.

bullets.title: DIS: Earnings preview Nov 17 — bulls cite SVOD margins >10% and ESPN highs; options imply 6.2% move
bullets.body: DIS Q4 consensus is $25.16B revenue / $1.68 EPS with FY27 guidance for double-digit adjusted EPS growth. Bull case: SVOD margins crossing 10%, record Experiences results, ESPN viewership at 10-year high. Bear case: structural sports-rights cost pressure, secular linear TV decline, soft Asia parks. Jefferies flags DIS at 52-week high with potential breakout targeting $140+ on FY27 cost savings. Options imply ~6.2% post-earnings move.

bullets.title: APP: Jefferies top '27 Internet pick — 'Axon 2.0' e-commerce customer ramp viewed as material Q4 catalyst
bullets.body: Jefferies positions APP for a breakthrough Q4'26 with new e-commerce customer growth and model rollout described as 'Axon 2.0' material. APP appears in JPM's note as an SMID Internet name abandoned by generalists. Sector sentiment in SMID Internet is worse than software with only specialists remaining.

bullets.title: GOOGL: TPU shipments 8-9M units in 2027 per Ming-Chi Kuo; gaining AI search share at 25.6% of citations
bullets.body: JPM estimates GOOGL TPU shipments of 8-9M units in 2027, 14-15M in 2028, 16-18M in 2029 (via Ming-Chi Kuo). Piper notes GOOGL is gaining AI search share notably at 25.6% of citations among the top 1,000 domains. Citi maintains Buy on GOOGL; Google also acquired a pre-developed Wyoming data center site with hybrid power plan.

bullets.title: TSLA: JPM flags robotaxi traction building; Cybercab sales begin despite federal safety probe
bullets.body: JPM published dedicated robotaxi research flagging building traction for TSLA's autonomous vehicle program. Separately, macro headlines confirm Tesla began autonomous Cybercab sales despite an ongoing federal safety probe.

bullets.title: VKTX: Oppenheimer bullish at $120 PT — VK2735 shows ~22% weight loss at week 33 with 97% retention
bullets.body: Oppenheimer reiterates VKTX with $120 PT, highlighting VK2735's retatrutide-like efficacy (~22% weight loss at week 33) with tirzepatide-like tolerability and 97% patient retention on maintenance. Every-other-week and monthly dosing options plus an oral formulation address treatment discontinuation/weight-regain issues that plague the obesity category.

bullets.title: NET: RBC bullish post-earnings; Wolfe Research includes in Agentic Infra basket (SNOW, TWLO, DDOG, NET)
bullets.body: RBC lists NET in its post-Q3 bullish software bucket alongside MSFT and TEAM. Wolfe Research is 'long and strong' on the Agentic Infra basket (TWLO, DDOG, SNOW, NET) going into week. All-Security SaaS index trades at 8.1x FY+2 EV/Sales with multiples down 3.57% W/W.

bullets.title: HIMS: JPM digital tracker — HIMS October DAUs +1% Y/Y (improving from -5% in Sept); GLP-1 search softening
bullets.body: HIMS October DAUs improved to +1% Y/Y from -5% in September, but HERS DAUs remain deeply negative at -24% Y/Y. Google Search interest in peptides and branded GLP-1 offerings continued to soften into October across all categories, adding to deceleration risk for the GLP-1 compounding business.

bullets.title: VZ & T: FCC Upper C-Band auction (Apr 2027) — JPM forecasts $53B spend; VZ to lead at $15-20B
bullets.body: FCC released final Upper C-Band auction procedures with bidding starting Apr 27, 2027. JPM maintains ~$53B total spend forecast at $1.00/MHz-pop. Verizon expected to be most aggressive at $15-20B given smallest sub-6 GHz position; T-Mobile $10-15B; AT&T $5-10B (less need post-EchoStar deal). SpaceX (up to $10B) is the largest swing factor. Spending is manageable for incumbent balance sheets but could slow buybacks or deleveraging, particularly at VZ.

bullets.title: CRWV: Hedge funds added >1 std of shorts; CoreWeave beat with >900MW additional contracted power QoQ
bullets.body: UBS crowding data shows hedge funds added more than 1 standard deviation of CRWV shorts even as CoreWeave beat revenue/guidance with >900MW additional contracted power QoQ and ~$9B prepayments covering 75% of 2027 capex. CRWV is down 6.8% in Monday premarket alongside broader neo-cloud/AI infrastructure weakness.

bullets.title: MSFT: Global outage Friday; Ignite (Nov 18) expected to feature agentic AI product announcements
bullets.body: MSFT suffered a global outage Friday but remains recommended by UBS for defense despite crowding. Morgan Stanley is hosting a group breakfast at MSFT Ignite on Nov 18; Wolfe Research expects agentic product announcements and AI messaging. RBC lists MSFT in its post-Q3 bullish software bucket.

bullets.title: FSLR: Removed from OPCO buy list; down 10.6% on the week, -34.4% YTD
bullets.body: FSLR was removed from Oppenheimer's large-cap 50/50 buy list this week. The stock declined 10.6% for the week ended Nov 13 and is down 34.4% YTD, making it among the worst S&P 500 performers year-to-date.

bullets.title: SPOT: Jefferies top '27 pick — 20%+ FCF growth via price increases, opex moderation, new monetization
bullets.body: Jefferies positions SPOT for 20%+ FCF growth through price increases, operating expense moderation, and new product monetization. SPOT was added to Oppenheimer's large-cap buy list this week alongside PLTR, TXN, MSI, and VRSN as part of a shift toward higher-quality businesses.

bullets.title: AMZN: Lost 40 Leo satellites in ULA Vulcan rocket failure; AI agents disrupting BKNG, EXPE, AMZN, ETSY
bullets.body: Amazon lost 40 Project Kuiper (Leo) satellites in a Boeing-Lockheed ULA Vulcan rocket failure, a material setback for its satellite broadband ambitions. Separately, JPM flags AI Search/AI Overviews/AI agents as a structural disruptor to AMZN, BKNG, EXPE, and ETSY, with generalist investors having abandoned SMID Internet names in favor of specialists.
